sections.h2: What sets the Town of Oyster Bay apart for a home seller?
sections.html:
The Town of Oyster Bay is the easternmost of Nassau County's three towns and the only one that stretches from the Long Island Sound shore to the South Shore. It covers about 169.5 square miles, and roughly 38 percent of that is water. The North Shore is hilly, the South Shore has sandy beaches and the land between is a plain (Wikipedia).

Inside those borders sit 18 villages and 18 hamlets, served by 20 post offices and 30 ZIP codes. Each post office shares a name with one of those places, but their boundaries usually do not match, so your mailing address may not name the village or hamlet your lot is in. Start with the section, block and lot number on your tax bill and ask the town whether your house falls in a village.

English settlers made their first land purchase in Oyster Bay in 1653, the settlement received its charter in 1667, and Nassau County was created in 1899, a year after western Queens County became part of New York City. Sagamore Hill, the former residence of Theodore Roosevelt, is in the village of Cove Neck and is now a museum.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Oyster Bay homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 301,115 people in the town on July 1, 2025 and counted 100,559 households for 2020 to 2024. About 89.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $708,600 and median gross rent is $2,572 (QuickFacts).

  • Median household income: $160,126 in 2024 dollars
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $3,910
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 55.6 percent
  • Residents in the same house a year earlier: 93.3 percent
  • Mean travel time to work: 34.9 minutes

With an owner rate near 90 percent, most homes here are lived in by their owners, so ask your lender for a payoff figure early in any sale.

sections.h2: When are Oyster Bay property taxes due?
sections.html:
Oyster Bay taxes come in two bills, a school bill mailed in October and a general bill mailed in January, each payable in two halves. The Receiver of Taxes lists the penalty-free windows below, and homeowners with an escrow account have the bills sent to their lender (Receiver of Taxes FAQ).

BillDuePaid without penalty through
General tax, first halfJanuary 1February 10
General tax, second halfJuly 1August 10
School tax, first halfOctober 1November 10
School tax, second halfApril 1May 10

Source: Town of Oyster Bay Receiver of Taxes.

Miss the window and a 1 percent monthly penalty applies, retroactive to the original due date. When collection closes, on May 31 for school taxes and August 31 for general taxes, unpaid bills move to the Nassau County Treasurer. A bill marked Arrears in the upper left corner means that has already happened. The office takes payments at Town Hall North in Oyster Bay, Town Hall South in Massapequa, by mail and online, and only a United States Postal Service postmark proves a payment was mailed on time.

New owners should tell the Receiver in writing so the next bill reaches them. Banks, title companies and attorneys paying for someone else owe a $10 duplicate bill fee with each payment, which is worth raising when the closing statement is prepared.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Nassau County assessment from Oyster Bay?
sections.html:
You file with Nassau County rather than the town, and the deadline is March 1. The state tax department says Nassau's Assessment Review Commission meets throughout the year but complaints must be filed by that date, and the form and instructions come from the commission (tax.ny.gov). It is a different calendar from the town boards that hold a spring Grievance Day elsewhere in the state.

The Receiver's FAQ points out that home improvements may change an assessment through the Nassau County Department of Assessment in Mineola. If you added a dormer, finished a basement or built a deck, a new buyer's tax bill may differ from yours. Ask the county for the assessment on file and compare it with the work you did.

sections.h2: What does the Nassau County Clerk require to record a deed?
sections.html:
The Nassau County Clerk at 240 Old Country Road in Mineola records deeds and indexes them by the property's section, block and lot. A wrong or missing number is the most common reason a document is rejected, and the clerk does not verify it, so copy it from the current county tax bill (Land Recording Guide).

  • Documents must be notarized, legible and signed in original ink, with names matching exactly between the heading and the acknowledgment.
  • Post office boxes are not accepted as addresses.
  • Transfer tax must be paid by certified check, and recording fees can go by personal check or Visa or MasterCard.
  • Documents should be presented at least an hour before the closing.
  • E-recording is available through three approved companies, which title firms and attorneys typically use.

Forms TP-584 and RP-5217 accompany the deed. A nonresident seller who owes estimated income tax on the gain files Form IT-2663 and pays that tax to the recording officer when the deed is filed. The guide is dated October 2022, so confirm fees on the clerk's website before the closing.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does an Oyster Bay seller owe?
sections.html:
New York's tax is $2 for each $500 of the price, rounded up, and the seller pays it by default (tax.ny.gov). At the town's median owner-occupied value of $708,600, the rounded price is $709,000, which is 1,418 units and $2,836. Ask the Nassau County Clerk whether any county or local charge applies to your deed, because the rate on the state page is only the statewide piece.

The additional 1 percent mansion tax applies when a residence sells for $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it. Sellers should still read the contract, since parties may agree to shift the base tax, and the state keeps joint liability if the tax goes unpaid.

sections.h2: What disclosures and permits matter on an Oyster Bay sale?
sections.html:
A one to four family seller must deliver a signed property condition disclosure statement before the buyer signs a binding contract (Real Property Law 462). For a town with a long Sound and bay shoreline, the flood section is the part buyers read closely. It asks about FEMA floodplain and flood hazard zones, flood insurance, elevation certificates, past flood claims, sump pumps and water entering the structure from storm surge or tidal inundation.

Building permits run through the town's Department of Planning and Development, and application forms are posted at oysterbaytown.com/building. Before listing, make a list of past work such as pools, fences, generators and solar panels, and confirm each was permitted. The form also asks about certificates of occupancy, and an unclosed permit is easier to fix before a contract than after.

sections.h2: Does a cash offer make sense for an Oyster Bay house?
sections.html: It can, when time matters more than top price. A cash purchase leaves out the buyer's lender, so the schedule rests on payoffs, the tax clearance steps above and recording in Mineola. Have your last tax receipt, deed and any open permit paperwork ready before you ask for a number.

faqs.q: When is the first half of Oyster Bay general tax due?
faqs.a: It is due January 1 and can be paid without penalty through February 10. The second half is due July 1 and payable through August 10. The school bill follows its own schedule, with October 1 and April 1 due dates.

faqs.q: What happens to Oyster Bay taxes I do not pay by the deadline?
faqs.a: A 1 percent penalty per month applies, counted back to the original due date. After May 31 for school taxes and August 31 for general taxes, unpaid amounts are payable to the Nassau County Treasurer instead of the Receiver of Taxes.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to challenge an Oyster Bay assessment?
faqs.a: March 1. Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission takes complaints through that date, according to the state tax department. For Nassau properties the state sends owners to the county commission for forms, deadlines and instructions.

faqs.q: What number must appear on a Nassau County deed?
faqs.a: The section, block and lot, plus a unit number for a condominium. The clerk's guide says it belongs on the first page and can be copied from the current tax bill. Errors here cause more rejected filings than any other mistake.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer pay the mansion tax on a $1.2 million Oyster Bay sale?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it. The mansion tax is 1 percent of the price on a residence sold for $1 million or more, and the seller owes it only if the buyer fails to pay. The base transfer tax of $2 per $500 is the seller's by default.
